pr_title: eth/downloader: fixes data race between synchronize and other methods
pr_body:
There was a race condition between `downloader.synchronize()` and `Progress` `syncWithPeer` `fetchHeight` `findAncestors` and `processHeaders`
This PR changes the behavior of the downloader a bit.
Previously the functions `Progress` `syncWithPeer` `fetchHeight` `findAncestors` and `processHeaders` read the syncMode anew within their loops. Now they read the syncMode at the start of their function and don't change it during their runtime. 

I think this is safe, as we shouldn't switch the syncMode while they are running, and if so we shouldn't react to the switch but keep on running the syncMode that we started with.

cc @mvdan 
(hopefully) fixes https://github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/21196

issue_context.title: eth/downloader: Progress is racy while a node is syncing
issue_context.body:

If you want to reproduce the crash locally, you can check out https://gitlab.com/vocdoni/go-dvote/-/tree/eth-downloader-race, and do `cd test && go test -race -vet=off -run Web3WS -v`. It panics pretty consistently for me in 10-20s.

Of course, I don't want you to debug my codebase. The test does a bunch of stuff, but in the end, it's really just starting an ethereum node and getting its downloader progress repeatedly.

I think this is a bug in go-ethereum; `Downloader.Progress` reads the `mode` field, which is modified by `Downloader.synchronise`. Calls to `synchronise` seem to be done by the started node on its own; we aren't calling the method directly. `Progress` does use a mutex, but that only seems to guard the "sync stats" fields, not `mode`.
